title: Squares & Square Roots
description: Class 8 IMO — Squares & square roots: perfect squares and their properties, finding squares and square roots by prime factorisation and long division, and Pythagorean triplets.

topics.title: Perfect Squares & Their Properties
topics.concept: A perfect square is a number that is the square of a whole number, like 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. A perfect square can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9 — never in 2, 3, 7 or 8.

examples.problem: Can a number ending in 7 be a perfect square?
examples.solution: No — perfect squares never end in 2, 3, 7 or 8.

recap: Perfect square = the square of a whole number.
Perfect squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9.

quiz.q: Which of these is a perfect square?
A perfect square can never end in which digit?
quiz.explanation: Perfect squares never end in 2, 3, 7 or 8 — so 8.

topics.title: Finding Squares & Square Roots
topics.concept: The square root of a number is the value that, when multiplied by itself, gives that number. We can find it by prime factorisation (pairing factors) or by long division. For example, √196 = 14 and √225 = 15.
recap: Square root: the number that multiplies by itself to give the value.
Use prime factorisation (pairing) or long division.

topics.title: Pythagorean Triplets
topics.concept: A Pythagorean triplet is three whole numbers a, b, c with a² + b² = c². Examples are (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13) and (8, 15, 17). For any whole number m, (2m, m² − 1, m² + 1) is a triplet.
recap: A triplet satisfies a² + b² = c².

questions.q: A perfect square can never end in which digit?
questions.explanation: Perfect squares never end in 2, 3, 7 or 8.
